My mind clouded, I settled down into a fitful slumber. Occasionally waking up with a start (well, not really "waking up," see I hadn't gotten to actually sleep yet), I screamed and panted. Every knock of the tree branch on my window forced me to jump. The wood settled in the house, a few creaks and moans as my curtains fluttered in the breeze.

I suppose I could have closed the window, but the air felt nice. Eventually I lost track of time and fell deep into sleep. As I dreamed, the knocks and the creaks still prevailed. But, it was a dream, I reckoned. At least I hoped it was.

I was lost. A winding road, cracked and forgotten by cars, stretched out before me. Onward, I supposed. I began to walk, all the while the rustling coming from behind me. Around me, overgrown farmland. Probably abandoned. Weird, I thought.

That's when I noticed the wooded area ahead. The road went right through it, just forested and dark. As I drew closer, I saw what appeared to be five others, just standing. I approached them and they turned around. Each of them were wearing a different color leather jacket; each of them overwhelmed by fear.

"Guys, Red's here." Yellow spoke first. He was a handsome young man, dark skin and an infectious smile. He was clearly afraid, but trying to ease the others. White approached me, her long blonde hair tied behind her.

"What do you think we should do?" She asked. Instinctively, She went to Violet's side. Violet just sat on the ground, staring pensively at the woods. He was a thin fellow, not unfit, just lean. He adjusted his glasses.

"Can any of you remember your name?" He looked around at the others. Green, the youngest of us, shook his head. He couldn't have been more than 17.

"No. I'm beginning to wonder if this isn't a dream." Green picked up a leaf. "It's too real."

"I remember my name," I piped in.

"Oh! Great!" Yellow exclaimed, smiling brightly. "What is it?"

I paused. Trying to speak my name my voice went silent.

"...Red." is all that managed to escape my mouth.

"Oh... You're having the same issue I am then." Chimed in Blue. She tucked her shord auburn hair behind her ears. "I say we go back."

"Then we wouldn't go on the journey we're supposed to be on." Violet stared at the woods.

"Um... Yellow?" I immediately felt a connection with Yellow. He approached me first. Yellow turned to me, then looked at what I was staring at.

The road was gone from behind us. I looked back at the forested area, then at the others.

Yellow. Blue. White. Violet. Green. And I was Red. And This wasn't a dream.

"Then we press onward." I said. We had a path going forward, and nothing behind us. The others shifted uneasily. "Look, as long as we stick together, we'll be safe. Does anyone have any weapons?"

We searched our pockets. Nothing.

Yellow stepped forward. "Alright. She's right. Nothing behind us. So let's not sit here forever. Red and I will go in front and warn you all about anything. Blue and Violet, stick to the rear and watch our backs. Green, White. Stay in the middle." The others agreed. While he was speaking I found two nice sized branches. I handed one to him. I smiled, trying to stay positive, like he was.

"As long as we stick together." And onward we went. The sun set somewhere behind us and it grew increasinly hard to see.

The lights dimmed, and the rustling grew louder. Out in front of us, I could see two human figures. I pointed them out to Yellow, indicating we should stay silent. As we grew closer, I could see they were just corpses, hanging some 2 feet off the ground. Instinctively, I covered Green's eyes, and Yellow Shielded White. That's when the creature emerged.

THis must be Black, I thought. Or it was.

Grinning in the darkness, I could see his shining, pointed teeth and glowing amber eyes come up from the forest's black background. I swung at him, my branch colliding with his torso and breaking. Yellow grabbed my hand and ran. We all ran.

As long as we're together.

The darkness was behind us. Blue and Violet shouted to go faster, but the increasing weight was so hard to keep up with. Every step was a chore.

Finally, we reached the edge of the forest. We cheered, figuring it was the end.

That's when it all went black.

As light emerged, I opened my eyes. I was still clutching Yellow's hand. But it was different. We were all in a building now. Yellow nodded and whispered to me

"Don't be afraid, as long as we're together."

When I looked over, I saw the dark beast come closer.

"I have a game for you." It said. "One that requires... a bit of fun. Each of you are going to be placed in a challenge. If you survive, then you get to leave. If not.... well."

I screamed as a white hot surge bursts through my arm, but I never let go of Yellow. When I looked down, after the pain had stopped, I was only clutching a tiny yellow disk in place of his hand. He was gone. And I was in the same room.

"As for you." The creature said. "I think I'll have a bit of fun with you."
